headline: Brayan Bello deals and the Red Sox keep the heat on
morning_brew: Brayan Bello was absolute nails yesterday, keeping the Angels quiet for five innings while the offense provided enough pop to secure another win at Fenway. Watching him rack up seven strikeouts without giving up a single run was a pure joy, and it felt like he was in complete control of the strike zone from the moment he stepped on the hill. It was a clean, professional outing that kept our rhythm intact and gave the guys in the dugout plenty of reason to stay aggressive at the plate. Seeing the starting rotation turn in that kind of performance makes the whole team look like they are playing with a dangerous level of confidence right now.

The bullpen had to step up to bridge the gap, and while things got a little bit interesting in the middle frames, Garrett Whitlock locked the door with a pair of punchouts to seal the deal. Adley Rutschman provided the big spark we needed with his home run, and it is exactly that kind of timely hitting that separates a good team from a true contender during this stretch run. My mother called me after the final out and just laughed, saying she actually enjoyed watching a game that did not require her to hide behind a sofa cushion. That is the kind of stress-free baseball I can get behind as we keep chasing down the spots we need to lock in.

The schedule stays packed starting with tonight's matchup against the Angels, and I am choosing to focus entirely on the nine innings ahead of us rather than worrying about the divisional standings. We are holding a spot in the hunt and I am keeping my head down, trusting the momentum we have built over this winning streak to carry us forward. My neighbor Rick has moved on from his umpire dossier to investigating the stadium lights, claiming they are calibrated differently when we play under the night sky, but I am just planning on enjoying the game and hoping for another win to keep the Duck Boat fund growing.
